## Fixes
- **ArrHub no longer stops on a malformed request** – a single invalid request (e.g. from a network scanner or bot) could make the server exit. It now answers `400 Bad Request`, logs the request and keeps running.
- **Crash guard** – any unexpected error is written to the log with a timestamp and ArrHub keeps running instead of exiting.
- **Broken redirects** – a service with *Accept self-signed certificate* or an own CA that answered with an invalid redirect address could crash the server; it now shows a normal connection error on the card.
- **No overlapping refreshes** – the browser waits for the previous status refresh to finish before starting the next one, so a slow service no longer gets a pile-up of requests from every open tab.

## Upgrade

**Docker**
```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/moordrak/arrhub:1.9.1   # or :latest
docker compose up -d                          # if you use docker-compose.yml
```

**Proxmox LXC** (on the Proxmox host)
```bash
pct exec <CTID> -- bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moordrak/arrhub/main/install.sh)"
```

**Debian / Ubuntu**
```bash
bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moordrak/arrhub/main/install.sh)"
```

Your existing `config.json` is kept.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/moordrak/arrhub/compare/v1.9.0...v1.9.1
